title: Can Old Tests Do New Tricks for Resolving SWE Issues?
read_source: https://arxiv.org/html/2510.18270v2; ACM DOI 10.1145/3808148 verified in article metadata and artifact README
datasets: For reproduction-test scoring they use TDD-Bench Verified harness but evaluate the Lite 300 and Verified 500 cohorts for consistency; SWT-Bench is discussed as related work/harness comparison, not the evaluated benchmark. No Defects4J or BugsInPy experiment.
task: Issue-based regression-test localization/minimization (TestPrune/TestLoc) from issue descriptions plus repository, followed by use of selected old tests as context for Otter++ reproduction-test generation, Agentless patch selection, and SWE-agent/Trae Agent patch validation.
input_setting: For each SWE-Bench issue and buggy repository, LLM identifies suspicious files/functions, selects up to 10 test files, coverage runs map existing passing tests to suspicious source lines, and greedy-additional/greedy-total set-cover variants reduce the test set. Selected tests are exposed to downstream reproduction/repair workflows. The minimizer does not receive the golden patch; golden buggy/fixed patch lines are used for evaluation ground truth.
author_relationship_evidence: The repository README states it is the artifact for “Can Old Tests do New Tricks for Resolving SWE Issues?”, accepted at FSE 2026, and describes the complete TestLoc pipeline, pre-computed results, and all-instance scripts. IBM/Issue-Test-Localizer source was checked at main HEAD b9100eb6a4550486a26a07704d2d93560eaf751e. The paper’s author/corresponding-authors include IBM; repository organization and README directly match the paper.
source_commit_or_archive: https://github.com/IBM/Issue-Test-Localizer/tree/b9100eb6a4550486a26a07704d2d93560eaf751e (HEAD pinned by `git ls-remote`; no release tag observed). Static files inspected at this commit: README.md, LICENSE, requirements.txt, src/run_pipeline.py, src/model_config.py, src/localization.py, src/test_file_selection.py, src/test_minimization.py, and src/minimization.sh.
license: Apache-2.0; repository has LICENSE and GitHub resource badge.
exact_models: TestPrune localization/test-file retrieval/tie-break calls use GPT-4o and Claude-3.7-Sonnet, temperature 0.8. Source passes model IDs as CLI args; `src/model_config.py` default temperature is 0.8.

Downstream comparisons: Otter with GPT-4o and Claude-3.7-Sonnet; Agentless with Claude-Sonnet-3.7 and GPT-4o; SWE-agent with Claude-Sonnet-4 on Lite; Trae Agent with Claude-Sonnet-3.7 on Verified (test-time scaling disabled for Trae). Artifact README single-instance sample pins `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`; default full-run example uses that model.
weights_status: No fine-tuned weights required/reported. Paper uses hosted GPT-4o/Anthropic Claude models and open-source agent frameworks. Artifact supports Anthropic, OpenAI and OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints. API snapshots/availability are not independently revalidated here; no model calls made.
evaluation_route: Read the complete 13,000-word arXiv v2 full-text export, including main sections 1–8 and conclusion; paper DOI 10.1145/3808148 and FSE 2026 artifact identity verified against the author repository. Inspect artifact README, Apache-2.0 license, dependency list, model client, pipeline/localization/test-selection/minimization code and shell entrypoint at pinned commit. README supplies precomputed regression/reproduction/agent/Agentless outputs, quick-start demo (3–5 min for one task), and reports full SWE-Bench Verified pipeline about 2 days; paper reports TestPrune reduces test count >1,000x and runtime 27x, precision .63, coverage recall .71. Table 1 absolute F→P gains are +1.6–2.8 percentage points (e.g. 31.2→34.0), while paper’s 6.2–9.0% wording is relative improvement. Agentless/agent resolution results include relative lifts; do not confuse these with percentage-point lifts. No source execution, API use, reproduction, or modifications performed.
blockers: Full-scale exact evaluation requires Docker/SWE-bench images, Python project environments, coverage.py dynamic contexts, datasets and about two days of pipeline runtime for Verified; exact resource requirements are environment-dependent.

Paper uses paid hosted GPT-4o and Claude APIs (estimated TestPrune overhead $0.02/$0.05 per issue); reproducing downstream Otter/Agentless/SWE-agent/Trae comparisons adds substantial API/model cost. No calls made.

Model versions and API behavior can change; pin exact model identifiers from artifact and paper. A custom model endpoint is supported, but such a run is a custom-model evaluation, not an exact paper reproduction.
The paper’s benchmark is Python SWE-Bench Lite/Verified, not SWT-Bench, Defects4J or BugsInPy. SWT-Bench is only discussed; Java/Defects4J adaptation would be outside the paper reproduction.
The paper calls several relative gains “%”; compare the raw table before reporting them as percentage points.
concept_fit: High as issue-level test context/retrieval and bug-revealing-test support: issue → suspicious functions → existing tests covering suspicious lines → focused regression tests → new F→P reproduction tests or repair feedback. Selected test names/assertions can expose usage patterns and affected behaviors. It is not an explicit root-cause taxonomy, causal explanation model, or novel assertion generator; it uses coverage to localize relevant test suites.
recommendation: Promote to a top reproducible candidate for testing issue-based test retrieval/minimization and as an add-on to a BRT pipeline. Best fit for the user’s preference is SWT-Bench-like issue reproduction/bug discovery, though the paper itself uses SWE-Bench Lite/Verified and Python. Start from the author’s included outputs or a single-task run with the exact API model if authorized; compare our model through the supported custom endpoint as a separate evaluation. Do not call the latter exact reproduction. It provides suspicious-function context, not a root-cause taxonomy.
